# Rebecca 1.9.5

Rebecca 1.9.5 stops the panel from re-syncing every node every few seconds, keeps a failing host action from blocking a node's users, and repairs the outbound traffic table on databases moved from SQLite.

## Nodes

- A node builds the reply of a sync before it records the revision it just applied, so every successful sync looked one revision behind. The panel then queued another sync on every maintenance pass and re-applied the config on all nodes about every ten seconds, which kept outbounds such as WireGuard from staying connected. A successful sync now counts as applied at the revision that was sent.
- A runtime or geo update that failed with a retryable error was retried forever and held back every user and config operation queued behind it, so new users never reached the node. Host actions now give up after five attempts and no longer block the other operations of their node.

## Database

- Databases moved from SQLite to MySQL could keep a unique index on `outbound_traffic.outbound_id` alone, which made outbound traffic sync fail with a duplicate entry error when an outbound exists on the master and on nodes. After each migration run the panel drops such indexes, merges duplicate rows by summing their traffic and restores the unique key on `(target_id, outbound_id)`.

## Upgrade notes

> No schema version change in this release. The outbound traffic repair runs automatically on start.
